objects.description: Abstract byte sink interface in namespace snappy. Consumers implement Append and optionally GetAppendBuffer to receive compressed output efficiently. Non-copyable. Destructor is virtual. No direct ownership semantics beyond typical interface usage.
Abstract byte source interface in namespace snappy. Provides Available, Peek, and Skip to supply input to decompression or other consumers. Non-copyable. Virtual destructor.
Concrete Source that yields bytes from a flat memory buffer provided at construction. Maintains internal pointer and remaining byte count. Used to feed snappy operations from an in-memory array.
Concrete Sink that writes bytes to a caller-provided flat array without bounds checks. Caller must ensure sufficient space. Provides CurrentDestination to inspect the running output pointer.

functions.name: snappy::Compress
functions.description: Compresses bytes read from the given Source and appends the compressed data to the given Sink. Returns the number of bytes written to the sink. Typical usage is for streaming or zero-copy compression using custom Source/Sink implementations.
requirements: source must be a valid, initialized snappy::Source that can be read from until exhaustion.
sink must be a valid, initialized snappy::Sink that accepts appended data via Append()/GetAppendBuffer().

The lifetime of any buffers returned by sink->GetAppendBuffer() must respect the Sink contract (caller must call Append() with the returned pointer and the number of bytes written before any other Sink operation).
On failure conditions are not documented in this header; callers should assume it either throws no exceptions or signals errors via return value/underlying interfaces (unknown).

functions.name: snappy::GetUncompressedLength
functions.description: Reads the uncompressed length from the compressed stream header in source and stores it in *result. The actual uncompressed length may differ if the stream is truncated. After this call, the source is left in a state unsuitable for further operations (e.g., RawUncompress) unless the caller rewinds or recreates the Source.
requirements: source must be a valid, initialized snappy::Source positioned at the beginning of a Snappy-compressed stream.
result must be non-null.
Caller must rewind or recreate the Source before attempting subsequent operations like RawUncompress(), as this call leaves the Source in an unsuitable state for further operations.
Returns false on parse error; caller must check the return value before trusting *result.

functions.name: snappy::Uncompress
functions.signature: bool snappy::Uncompress(const char* compressed, size_t compressed_length, std::string* uncompressed)
functions.description: Decompresses the Snappy-compressed buffer [compressed, compressed+compressed_length) into *uncompressed, replacing its previous contents. Returns false if the input is corrupted and could not be decompressed.
requirements: compressed must point to at least compressed_length readable bytes.
uncompressed must be non-null.
compressed must not alias *uncompressed (explicitly required).
Caller must check the boolean return value to detect corruption/decompression failure.
Existing contents of *uncompressed are discarded.

functions.name: snappy::RawCompress
functions.signature: void snappy::RawCompress(const char* input, size_t input_length, char* compressed, size_t* compressed_length)
functions.description: Compresses the input byte array [input, input+input_length) into the caller-provided output buffer compressed. On return, *compressed_length is set to the number of bytes of compressed data produced.
requirements: input must point to at least input_length readable bytes.
compressed must point to a writable buffer of at least MaxCompressedLength(input_length) bytes (explicitly required).
compressed_length must be non-null and writable; it is set to the output size.
Caller manages the output buffer lifetime; there are no bounds checks performed beyond what the implementation does.

functions.name: snappy::RawUncompress
functions.signature: bool snappy::RawUncompress(const char* compressed, size_t compressed_length, char* uncompressed)
functions.description: Decompresses the Snappy-compressed buffer [compressed, compressed+compressed_length) directly into the caller-provided uncompressed buffer. Returns false if the message is corrupted and could not be decompressed.
requirements: compressed must point to at least compressed_length readable bytes produced by snappy::Compress/RawCompress.
uncompressed must point to a writable buffer large enough to hold the full uncompressed data (typically obtained via GetUncompressedLength()).
Caller must check the boolean return value to detect corruption/decompression failure.

functions.name: snappy::RawUncompressToIOVec
functions.signature: bool snappy::RawUncompressToIOVec(const char* compressed, size_t compressed_length, const struct iovec* iov, size_t iov_cnt)
functions.description: Decompresses the Snappy-compressed buffer [compressed, compressed+compressed_length) and writes the uncompressed bytes across the provided array of iovec buffers. Returns false if the message is corrupted and could not be decompressed.
requirements: compressed must point to at least compressed_length readable bytes produced by snappy::Compress/RawCompress.
iov must point to an array of iov_cnt buffers; if iov_cnt > 0, iov must be non-null.
The cumulative size of all iov buffers must be at least the full uncompressed length (GetUncompressedLength(compressed, compressed_length)).
Individual iov buffers must not overlap with each other (explicitly required).
Caller must check the boolean return value to detect corruption/decompression failure.

functions.name: snappy::MaxCompressedLength
functions.description: Returns the maximum possible size of the Snappy-compressed representation of an input of length source_bytes. Use this to size output buffers for RawCompress.
requirements: No special preconditions; source_bytes can be any size_t value. The result is an upper bound on compressed size.

functions.name: snappy::IsValidCompressedBuffer
functions.signature: bool snappy::IsValidCompressedBuffer(const char* compressed, size_t compressed_length)
functions.description: Checks whether the buffer [compressed, compressed+compressed_length) is a valid Snappy-compressed stream. Does not produce uncompressed data. Typically faster than full decompression.
requirements: compressed must point to at least compressed_length readable bytes.
Caller must check the boolean return value to determine validity.

functions.name: snappy::Sink::~Sink
functions.description: Virtual destructor for Sink. Allows proper cleanup via a base-class pointer.
requirements: No special requirements for callers; object must have been created by a matching constructor and not already destroyed.

functions.name: snappy::Sink::Append
functions.signature: virtual void snappy::Sink::Append(const char* bytes, size_t n) = 0
functions.description: Appends n bytes from bytes to the sink. Must be implemented by concrete Sink subclasses; used by compression routines to emit output.
requirements: bytes must point to at least n readable bytes.
Implementations must consume the data as part of the append operation.
Callers must respect any concrete Sink’s additional constraints, if any (unknown).

functions.name: snappy::Sink::GetAppendBuffer
functions.signature: virtual char* snappy::Sink::GetAppendBuffer(size_t length, char* scratch)
functions.description: Returns a writable buffer of at least length bytes for appending. The buffer is valid only until the next Sink operation. The default implementation returns scratch. After writing up to length bytes, the caller must call Append() with the returned pointer and the number of bytes actually written.
requirements: scratch must point to at least length writable bytes (since the default implementation returns scratch).
The caller must call Append() with the returned pointer and the number of bytes written before any other Sink operation.
If a non-scratch buffer is returned by an override, the caller may only pass a prefix of it to Append() and must not pass an interior pointer.

functions.name: snappy::Source::~Source
functions.description: Virtual destructor for Source. Allows proper cleanup via a base-class pointer.
requirements: No special requirements for callers; object must have been created by a matching constructor and not already destroyed.

functions.name: snappy::Source::Available
functions.description: Returns the number of bytes left to read from the source.
requirements: The Source object must be valid and initialized.
Implementations must ensure Available() accurately reflects unread bytes.

functions.name: snappy::Source::Peek
functions.description: Peeks at the next contiguous region of the source without advancing. Returns a pointer to the beginning of the region and stores its length in *len. The region is valid until the next call to Skip() or until the object is destroyed. The returned region may be larger than Available(); callers must only read Available() bytes.
requirements: len must be non-null.
Caller must not read more than Available() bytes even if *len is larger.
Any pointer returned becomes invalid after Skip(n) or destruction of the Source.

functions.name: snappy::Source::Skip
functions.description: Skips the next n bytes of the source. Invalidates any buffer returned by the previous Peek().
requirements: Available() must be >= n (explicitly required).
Caller must not use any previously returned Peek() buffer after calling Skip().

functions.name: snappy::ByteArraySource::ByteArraySource
functions.description: Constructs a Source that yields the contents of the flat array [p, p+n).
requirements: p must point to at least n readable bytes.
The memory referenced by p must remain valid and unchanged for the lifetime of the ByteArraySource or until all bytes have been consumed.

functions.name: snappy::ByteArraySource::~ByteArraySource
functions.description: Destructor for ByteArraySource.
requirements: No special requirements for callers.

functions.name: snappy::ByteArraySource::Available
functions.description: Returns the number of unread bytes remaining in the underlying array.
requirements: Object must be valid and constructed with a proper pointer/length.

functions.name: snappy::ByteArraySource::Peek
functions.description: Returns a pointer to the next contiguous unread region in the underlying array and stores its length in *len. The region is valid until Skip() or destruction, and may be larger than Available(); callers must only read Available() bytes.
requirements: len must be non-null.
Caller must not read more than Available() bytes even if *len is larger.
Pointer becomes invalid after Skip() or destruction.

functions.name: snappy::ByteArraySource::Skip
functions.description: Advances the read position by n bytes in the underlying array, invalidating any buffer returned by the previous Peek().
requirements: Available() must be >= n (inherits Source contract).

functions.name: snappy::UncheckedByteArraySink::UncheckedByteArraySink
functions.description: Constructs a Sink that writes to a caller-provided flat array without performing bounds checks. The sink maintains an internal current write pointer into dest.
requirements: dest must be a non-null pointer to writable memory large enough to hold all bytes that will be appended through this sink.
Caller is responsible for ensuring no out-of-bounds writes occur (no bounds checks are performed).

functions.name: snappy::UncheckedByteArraySink::~UncheckedByteArraySink
functions.description: Destructor for UncheckedByteArraySink.
requirements: No special requirements for callers.

functions.name: snappy::UncheckedByteArraySink::Append
functions.signature: virtual void snappy::UncheckedByteArraySink::Append(const char* data, size_t n)
functions.description: Appends n bytes from data to the current destination pointer, advancing the pointer. Performs no bounds checks.
requirements: data must point to at least n readable bytes.
The underlying destination buffer must have at least n bytes of free space; caller is responsible for sizing.
Unsafe: no bounds checks are enforced.

functions.name: snappy::UncheckedByteArraySink::GetAppendBuffer
functions.description: Returns a writable buffer for appending. For UncheckedByteArraySink, this typically returns the current destination pointer. After writing up to len bytes, the caller must call Append() with the returned pointer and the actual number of bytes written.
requirements: If the sink returns scratch, scratch must have at least len writable bytes.
Caller must ensure the underlying destination has sufficient capacity for len bytes when using the returned pointer.
Caller must call Append() with the returned pointer before any other Sink operation.

functions.name: snappy::UncheckedByteArraySink::CurrentDestination
functions.description: Returns the current destination pointer so the caller can determine how many bytes have been produced/written so far. Not a Sink interface method.
requirements: The sink must be valid; returned pointer is only meaningful with knowledge of the originally supplied destination buffer and how much has been written.

A byte sequence formatted according to the Snappy compression format. Begins with a varint-encoded uncompressed length followed by one or more Snappy chunks (literals and copy operations). Intended to be consumed by Snappy validators and decompression routines; arbitrary bytes may be rejected as invalid.

import os
import random
import struct
from typing import List

# This generator produces valid and interesting arbitrary binary data that
# targets snappy usage in the stubs:
# - Raw/Compress paths benefit from inputs with varying entropy, runs, and sizes
# - Source-related stubs only require any bytes; we still vary shapes
# - Keep size <= 2048 (stubs clamp); we select diverse lengths within that bound
# - Include patterns likely to trigger distinct compression paths (repeats, small alphabets,
#   gradually changing bytes, embedded zeros, ASCII text, random noise, mixed blocks)

MAX_TOTAL = 2048

def _rand(r: random.Random, a: int, b: int) -> int:
    return r.randint(a, b)

def _pick(r: random.Random, seq):
    return seq[r.randrange(len(seq))]

def _chunk_runs(r: random.Random, target_len: int) -> bytes:
    # Long repeated runs with varying run lengths and byte values
    out = bytearray()
    while len(out) < target_len:
        val = r.randrange(256)
        run = _rand(r, 1, min(512, target_len - len(out)))
        out.extend([val] * run)
    return bytes(out[:target_len])

def _chunk_low_entropy_alphabet(r: random.Random, target_len: int) -> bytes:
    # Small alphabet (e.g., 2-6 distinct bytes) with biased distribution
    alphabet_size = _rand(r, 2, 6)
    alphabet = [r.randrange(256) for _ in range(alphabet_size)]
    weights = [r.random() + 0.1 for _ in range(alphabet_size)]
    total_w = sum(weights)
    cum = []
    acc = 0.0
    for w in weights:
        acc += w / total_w
        cum.append(acc)
    out = bytearray()
    for _ in range(target_len):
        u = r.random()
        idx = 0
        while idx < len(cum) and u > cum[idx]:
            idx += 1
        out.append(alphabet[min(idx, len(alphabet)-1)])
    return bytes(out)

def _chunk_gradient(r: random.Random, target_len: int) -> bytes:
    # Slowly changing sequence, cycles through 0-255 with jitter
    start = r.randrange(256)
    step = _rand(r, 1, 5)
    jitter = _rand(r, 0, 3)
    out = bytearray()
    cur = start
    for i in range(target_len):
        if jitter and (i % _rand(r, 2, 7) == 0):
            cur = (cur + _rand(r, -jitter, jitter)) & 0xFF
        out.append(cur & 0xFF)
        cur = (cur + step) & 0xFF
    return bytes(out)

def _chunk_ascii_text(r: random.Random, target_len: int) -> bytes:
    # English-like ASCII with spaces, punctuation, newlines
    words = [
        b"the", b"and", b"to", b"of", b"a", b"in", b"that", b"is", b"for", b"on",
        b"snappy", b"compress", b"decompress", b"data", b"buffer", b"stream", b"chunk"
    ]
    punct = [b" ", b" ", b" ", b" ", b"\n", b". ", b", "]
    out = bytearray()
    while len(out) < target_len:
        w = _pick(r, words)
        # sometimes repeat a word to create runs
        reps = 1 if r.random() < 0.7 else _rand(r, 2, 8)
        for _ in range(reps):
            out.extend(w)
            out.extend(_pick(r, punct))
            if len(out) >= target_len:
                break
    return bytes(out[:target_len])

def _chunk_random(r: random.Random, target_len: int) -> bytes:
    return r.randbytes(target_len)

def _chunk_structured_blocks(r: random.Random, target_len: int) -> bytes:
    # Mix of sub-blocks: zeros, ones, small counters, patterned headers
    out = bytearray()
    while len(out) < target_len:
        choice = _rand(r, 0, 4)
        remain = target_len - len(out)
        blen = _rand(r, 1, min(256, remain))
        if choice == 0:
            out.extend(b"\x00" * blen)
        elif choice == 1:
            out.extend(b"\xFF" * blen)
        elif choice == 2:
            # counter
            start = r.randrange(256)
            out.extend(bytes(((start + i) & 0xFF) for i in range(blen)))
        elif choice == 3:
            # small repeating token
            tok_len = _rand(r, 1, min(8, blen))
            tok = r.randbytes(tok_len)
            reps = blen // tok_len
            out.extend(tok * reps + tok[: blen - reps * tok_len])
        else:
            # header-like prefix + payload
            hdr = struct.pack('<IHB', _rand(r,0,0xFFFFFFFF), _rand(r,0,0xFFFF), _rand(r,0,255))
            need = min(blen, remain)
            pay = r.randbytes(max(0, need - len(hdr)))
            out.extend((hdr + pay)[:need])
    return bytes(out[:target_len])

def _compose_mixed(r: random.Random, total_len: int) -> bytes:
    # Compose the final buffer by concatenating several chunks with varied characteristics
    chunkers = [
        _chunk_runs,
        _chunk_low_entropy_alphabet,
        _chunk_gradient,
        _chunk_ascii_text,
        _chunk_random,
        _chunk_structured_blocks,
    ]
    out = bytearray()
    # decide number of chunks 1..6
    n_chunks = _rand(r, 1, min(6, max(1, total_len // 16) + 1))
    remaining = total_len
    for i in range(n_chunks):
        if i == n_chunks - 1:
            blen = remaining
        else:
            # bias towards a range of sizes, including very small and medium blocks
            if remaining < 32:
                blen = remaining
            else:
                blen = _rand(r, 8, min(512, remaining - (n_chunks - i - 1)))
        chunker = _pick(r, chunkers)
        out.extend(chunker(r, blen))
        remaining = total_len - len(out)
        if remaining <= 0:
            break
    # Occasionally prepend or append tiny delimiters to vary boundaries
    if len(out) < total_len and r.random() < 0.3:
        pad = _pick(r, [b"", b"\x00", b"\x00\x00", b"\x01", b"\n"])  # keep valid arbitrary bytes
        out.extend(pad[: total_len - len(out)])
    return bytes(out[:total_len])

def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    r = random.Random(seed)
    # Choose a total length aligned with stub limits, emphasizing boundary cases
    lengths = [0, 1, 2, 3, 7, 8, 15, 16, 31, 32, 63, 64, 127, 128, 255, 256, 511, 512, 1023, 1024, 1536, 2048]
    if r.random() < 0.6:
        total_len = _pick(r, lengths)
    else:
        total_len = _rand(r, 0, MAX_TOTAL)
    # Build mixed content
    data = _compose_mixed(r, total_len)
    # Ensure bytes result and size bound
    return data[:MAX_TOTAL]

import random
import struct
from typing import List, Tuple

# This generator produces valid Snappy-compressed streams, focusing on simple
# literal-only blocks with a correct varint-encoded uncompressed length header.
# It aims to be accepted by:
# - snappy::GetUncompressedLength (parses header)
# - snappy::IsValidCompressedBuffer
# - snappy::Uncompress
# - snappy::RawUncompress (after header-driven allocation in the stub)
# The produced buffers are <= 2048 bytes (and well below 4096 as required).
#
# Snappy format basics used here:
# - Stream starts with Varint-encoded uncompressed length (little-endian 7-bit
#   groups, MSB=1 continuation except last byte where MSB=0).
# - Then a sequence of opcodes. We only emit literal opcodes (tag type 0).
#   Literal encoding:
#     tag byte: low 2 bits = 00 (literal), high 6 bits carry length code.
#     Let L be the literal length in bytes.
#       If 0 <= L-1 <= 59: tag = (L-1) << 2 | 0
#                          (no extra length bytes)
#       Elif 60 <= L-1 <= 0xFF + 60: tag = 60 << 2 | 0, then 1 byte: (L-1) as u8
#       Elif 0x100+60 <= L-1 <= 0xFFFF + 60: tag = 61 << 2 | 0, then 2 bytes little endian
#       Elif 0x10000+60 <= ... up to 4 extra bytes (we won't need > 2 here).
#   After the tag (and extra length bytes), L literal payload bytes follow.
# We avoid copy (back-reference) opcodes for simplicity while remaining valid.

MAX_TOTAL = 2048

# ---------------- Varint helpers ----------------

def _put_varint(n: int) -> bytes:
    if n < 0:
        raise ValueError("varint requires non-negative")
    out = bytearray()
    while True:
        b = n & 0x7F
        n >>= 7
        if n:
            out.append(b | 0x80)
        else:
            out.append(b)
            break
    return bytes(out)

# --------------- Literal encoding ----------------

def _encode_literal_chunk(data: bytes) -> bytes:
    L = len(data)
    assert L >= 0
    # Per spec, we encode literal length as (L-1)
    l_minus_1 = L - 1 if L > 0 else 0  # For L = 0, tag would be -1; avoid zero-length chunks entirely.
    if L == 0:
        # Avoid zero-length literal (unnecessary). Return empty.
        return b""

    if l_minus_1 <= 59:
        tag = (l_minus_1 << 2) | 0
        return bytes([tag]) + data
    elif l_minus_1 <= 0xFF + 60:
        tag = (60 << 2) | 0
        return bytes([tag, l_minus_1 - 60]) + data
    elif l_minus_1 <= 0xFFFF + 60:
        tag = (61 << 2) | 0
        val = l_minus_1 - 60
        return bytes([tag]) + struct.pack('<H', val) + data
    else:
        # Not expected for our size limits, but handle 3- and 4-byte length forms for completeness.
        if l_minus_1 <= 0xFFFFFF + 60:
            tag = (62 << 2) | 0
            val = l_minus_1 - 60
            return bytes([tag]) + val.to_bytes(3, 'little') + data
        else:
            tag = (63 << 2) | 0
            val = l_minus_1 - 60
            return bytes([tag]) + val.to_bytes(4, 'little') + data

# --------------- Content generation ----------------

def _random_bytes(rng: random.Random, n: int) -> bytes:
    # Mix of ASCII, zeros, high bytes to exercise different content densities
    chunks: List[bytes] = []
    remaining = n
    while remaining > 0:
        choice = rng.randrange(5)
        take = min(remaining, rng.randint(1, max(1, remaining)))
        if choice == 0:
            # ASCII letters
            s = bytes(rng.choice(b"abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyzABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZ0123456789 ") for _ in range(take))
        elif choice == 1:
            # Zero run
            s = b"\x00" * take
        elif choice == 2:
            # High-entropy random bytes
            s = rng.randbytes(take)
        elif choice == 3:
            # Repeating small pattern
            pat_len = rng.randint(1, 8)
            pat = rng.randbytes(pat_len)
            s = (pat * ((take + pat_len - 1)//pat_len))[:take]
        else:
            # UTF-8-like ASCII with newlines
            s = bytes(rng.choice(b"\n\r\t .,:;!?()[]{}<>+-=*/_%#@$") for _ in range(take))
        chunks.append(s)
        remaining -= take
    return b"".join(chunks)


def _make_uncompressed(rng: random.Random, target_max: int) -> bytes:
    # Generate an uncompressed payload with varied structure but bounded size.
    # Try to create 1..5 segments of varying lengths summing under target_max.
    segments: List[bytes] = []
    seg_count = rng.randint(1, 5)
    remaining = target_max
    for i in range(seg_count):
        if remaining <= 0:
            break
        # Bias towards a mix of small and medium segments
        base_max = min(remaining, rng.choice([8, 32, 64, 128, 256, remaining]))
        seg_len = rng.randint(1, base_max)
        segments.append(_random_bytes(rng, seg_len))
        remaining -= seg_len
    return b"".join(segments)

# --------------- Main generator ----------------

def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)

    # Choose an overall uncompressed size target, keeping total output <= 2048.
    # Account for header (<=5 bytes) and per-chunk tags. We'll be conservative.
    # Aim for uncompressed size up to ~1700 bytes.
    uncomp_target = rng.randint(0, 1700)

    # Sometimes pick specific edge-case sizes to exercise literal length encodings.
    edge_sizes = [0, 1, 60, 61, 255, 256, 257, 1024, 1500]
    if rng.random() < 0.35:
        uncomp_target = rng.choice(edge_sizes)

    uncompressed = _make_uncompressed(rng, uncomp_target)

    # Header: varint uncompressed length
    header = _put_varint(len(uncompressed))

    # Emit literals in chunks of varied sizes to hit different literal-length encodings.
    chunks: List[bytes] = [header]

    i = 0
    n = len(uncompressed)
    while i < n:
        # Choose chunk size with bias to cross thresholds for literal encodings
        remaining = n - i
        choices = [1, 15, 32, 60, 61, 62, 63, 64, 255, 256, 512]
        sz = rng.choice(choices)
        sz = max(1, min(sz, remaining))
        lit = uncompressed[i:i+sz]
        chunks.append(_encode_literal_chunk(lit))
        i += sz

    out = b"".join(chunks)

    # Ensure we remain within the harness limit. If exceeded (very unlikely with our caps),
    # trim the uncompressed payload and rebuild conservatively with one literal.
    if len(out) > MAX_TOTAL:
        uncompressed = uncompressed[:max(0, MAX_TOTAL - 10)]
        header = _put_varint(len(uncompressed))
        body = _encode_literal_chunk(uncompressed)
        out = header + body
        # If still too large (shouldn't be), truncate further
        if len(out) > MAX_TOTAL:
            trim = MAX_TOTAL - len(header) - 3
            trim = max(trim, 0)
            body = _encode_literal_chunk(uncompressed[:trim])
            out = header + body

    return out
